title: Surrealist, Maximalist Statement Shoes Are Having a Moment
summary: From faux fur to faux toes, here are a dozen pairs of sandals and boots in which to walk on the wild side.
body_text: Fashion Surrealist, Maximalist Statement Shoes Are Having a Moment From faux fur to faux toes, here are a dozen pairs of sandals and boots in which to walk on the wild side. by John Villa Pin Share Tweet Email If the viral (and insanely divisive) transparent footwear featured in June’s Saint Laurent men’s show made anything, ahem, clear, it’s that statement-making shoes are staging a comeback. The appetite for shocking fashion tends to rise and fall with the season, but funky footwear has been tiptoeing onto the market for years and seems to be here to stay. McQueen , Loewe and Dior are just a few brands pushing the boundaries of late, to great success. As surrealism and maximalism firm up their grip on consumers hungering for loud luxury, bizarre motifs are gaining a foothold in pumps, sandals and boots. For the Carrie Bradshaw–level shoe maven, vintage treasures in this vein abound. Here, we’ve compiled a selection of whimsical designer shoes that will speak to any eccentric collector’s sole. Maison Martin Margiela Tabi Boots The Margiela Tabi has perhaps the most fiercely debated silhouette in modern popular fashion. Introduced in 1988 by Martin Margiela , the boot was instantly a subversive success and a subject of traditionalist ridicule. Its bifucated toe, derived from 15th-century Japanese socks, has evolved into a token of cultural currency for fashion connoisseurs. This pair of Tabi boots, from 1995 , is hand-painted, as evidenced by the brush marks and ombré finish that climbs up to the ankle. Public opinion on Tabis will likely always be split, but that division just cements their icon status. Schiaparelli Trompe l’Oeil Sandals Elsa Schiaparelli famously turned shoes into headwear; Daniel Roseberry is turning them into art for (and of) the feet. Under Roseberry’s direction, shoes are some of Schiaparelli’s most coveted and outlandish accessories — just consider Zendaya’s couture bird heels and the hyperrealistic kitten slip-ons in the designer’s recent fall collection. Perhaps his most iconic footwear element is the gilded toe cap, like the ones on these trompe l’oeil sandals , molded to resemble toes. An additional attraction: This homage to the house’s long fascination with anatomy makes a fresh pedicure unnecessary. Prada Geisha Platforms From flames to fairies , Prada has long offered well-heeled fashionistas styles catering to their sense of adventure. These 2013 Prada embellished platforms whisk their wearer to the Far East, combining delicate florals with an homage to the traditional geta sandal. The double platform almost looks like a reverse reflection of a single sole, adding a dreamy architectural contrast to the feminine design. As a practical bonus, these are also likely the most comfortable shoes on this list. Giuseppe Zanotti Fish-Bone Sandals One man’s trash is Giuseppe Zanotti ’s treasure. The T-straps on these crystal-encrusted Piranha sandals are a glamorous take on discarded fish bones. The rows of bedazzled teeth on the ankle — these are piranha skeletons, after all — give the shoes an extra bite. And since Samantha Jones wore a pair (while covered in sushi) in the first Sex and the City movie , the sandals boast her coveted seal of approval. Versace x Haas Brothers Triple-Platform Bondage Boots Often, unexpected alliances produce the most thrilling outcomes. Take these triple-platform Bondage ankle boots from Versace ’s 2013 collaboration with the Haas Brothers . Versace is celebrated for endowing Italian fashion with glittering sex appeal, while the Haas Brothers are known for creating biomorphic, hallucinogenic fine art and design. These discordant influences converge with tantalizing drama in the Bondage boots. The strapped leather upper harks back to Gianni Versace’s famed Miss S&M collection, while the stacked, honeycomb-embossed platform alludes to organic motifs in the Haas Brothers’ signature gilded finish. Miu Miu Pink Faux-Fur and Crystal Block-Heel Sandals Miuccia Prada must have quite the sweet tooth. Miu Miu , Prada’s sister label, named after the designer, often displays a spritelier aesthetic than Prada itself, as witness these Miu Miu Fall/Winter 2017 sandals . The furry confections’ block heel, crystal clasp and exuberant faux-fur details scream delectable frivolity. Even on the feet, they can’t help calling to mind cotton candy. Vivienne Westwood Rocking Horse Shoes Vivienne Westwood ’s 1980s Rocking Horse shoes stand somewhere between closet staples and museum treasures. Introduced in the designer’s 1987 Harris Tweed collection, the wooden-platform footwear is part of fashion history. Beyond adding a few inches to the wearers’ height, the curved soles make them roll forward as they walk, evoking the motion of a child’s rocking horse. The ballet-slipper-inspired upper, with its crisscrossing laces, provides an additional hit of nostalgia. Alexander McQueen Oyster-Shell Wedge Sandals Sculptural, gravity-defying footwear is in the Alexander McQueen brand’s DNA. McQueen himself presented the world with a triumph of sci-fi fashion engineering in the 2010 Armadillo boot, and his mentee and successor, Sarah Burton, continued in his footsteps with the 2012 Oyster-Shell wedge . The sandals display the same aquatic-futurist sensibility that characterized the Plato’s Atlantis collection, which introduced the Armadillo. Their cantilevered heels gleam with a dramatic gold-and-black gradient, their sinuous forms recalling the polished ribs of a shell. The tentacle-like straps wind symmetrically up to the ankle, enclosing the foot in another dark, ethereal masterpiece from the house. Loewe Petal Brush Sandals In 2026, no discussion of unusual footwear would be complete without mentioning Loewe . During his tenure at the storied Spanish house, Jonathan Anderson revolutionized its aesthetic, making it synonymous with boundary-pushing illusionism. Techniques like trompe l’oeil and micromosaics elevated ready-to-wear fashion to Pop art, as in these Petal Brush heels from 2023. They belong to a collection in which nail-polish bottles, broken eggs and, in their case, fluffy makeup brushes stand in for stilettos, causing a double take from onlookers with every step. Christian Louboutin Spiked Kate Max Boots Dangerous might be used as an ironic word of praise for a pair of heels, but these Spiked Kate Max boots should actually be worn with caution. The Christian Louboutin creations feature a strip of chrome claws on the back of each shaft, which will probably make the person behind you take a step back. Although they are unlikely to cause any real injury, their intimidating effect is supremely satisfying. Balenciaga by Nicolas Ghesquière Gladiator Sandals Balenciaga’s Gladiator sandals became instant favorites in Rihanna’s fashion archive when she stepped out in them in 2008. Their bold chevron print, knee-high shin guards and rows of buckles are enhanced by colorful geometric enamel tiles on the heel that push the design even further into maximalist territory. Off-White by Virgil Abloh Meteor Shower Boots A natural disruptor, the late Virgil Abloh liked to poke holes in things. He challenged the status quo at Louis Vuitton Men’s and revolutionized streetwear with his own brand, Off-White . There, he poked literal holes in his Meteor Shower boots in 2020. The wedge heel and wide shaft create a futuristic look that evokes both moon landing and Swiss cheese. Whatever you see in them, ample foot ventilation is guaranteed. If only those clear Saint Laurents could say the same. Shop the Wonderfully Weird Collection View All About the author John Villa John Villa is the fashion specialist on 1stDibs’ Art and Design Research team, managing the curation and vetting of the marketplace’s fashion category. He holds a master’s degree in art history and visual culture from the University of Nottingham, but he now focuses on archival fashion history and the contemporary luxury market. Villa maintains an active presence on social media, where his fashion commentary and critiques have gained him more than 125,000 followers across TikTok and Youtube. In addition to his contributions to The Study , he also appears regularly on 1stDibs’s social media pages, presenting engaging video content on fashion history and trends. He is based in New York City. Pin Share Tweet Email Posted on July 30, 2026

body_text: View All News Ivonescimab Plus Chemotherapy Shows Consistent, Favorable Overall Survival Results in Western and Asian Patients in Updated Analysis from Global Phase III HARMONi Study July 22, 2026 Download (opens in new window) Western Patients Achieved OS HR of 0.76, Consistent with Asian Patients in this Global Phase III Study MIAMI--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Summit Therapeutics Inc. (Nasdaq: SMMT) today announced results of an updated overall survival (OS) analysis from the global Phase III HARMONi clinical trial featuring the novel, potential first-in-class investigational bispecific antibody ivonescimab. Ivonescimab plus platinum-doublet chemotherapy in this trial continues to show a positive OS trend and a consistent efficacy and safety profile in Asian and western patients when compared to chemotherapy alone. The HARMONi study is evaluating ivonescimab combined with chemotherapy compared to placebo plus chemotherapy in patients with endothelial growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) who were previously treated with a third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI). The study demonstrated a statistically significant benefit in the primary analysis for progression-free survival (PFS), one of the study’s two primary endpoints along with OS. Summit’s Biologics License Application (BLA) with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is based on the results from the HARMONi trial and has a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) goal action date of November 14, 2026. In April 2025, the primary OS analysis was performed, whereby ivonescimab in combination with chemotherapy showed a positive trend without achieving a statistically significant benefit with a hazard ratio of 0.79 (95% CI: 0.62 – 1.01; p=0.057). Median OS was 16.8 months for those patients administered ivonescimab plus chemotherapy vs. 14.0 months for those receiving placebo plus chemotherapy. At the time of the primary analysis, median follow-up time for western patients was 9.2 months and less than the median OS at the time of the primary analysis. In September 2025, an additional analysis was performed, whereby the western patients were followed to increase their time on study (Asian patients were included and locked at the time of the primary analysis at a median follow-up time of 32.7 months). This analysis included longer-term follow-up of western patients of 13.7 months. A hazard ratio of 0.78 (95% CI: 0.62 – 0.98; nominal p=0.0332) was observed, consistent with the primary analysis. Median OS remained the same in both arms from the primary analysis. An additional analysis was performed with a data cut-off date in June 2026, whereby most western patients have now discontinued treatment or completed two years of treatment. The median follow-up time for western patients now is 23.2 months. The cutoff date for Asian patients was consistent with the prior analysis with a median follow-up time of 32.7 months. A hazard ratio of 0.76 was observed in both the full intention-to-treat population and the subgroup of western patients. More detailed data from this analysis are intended to be presented at an upcoming medical meeting. These results have been made available to the FDA. With longer follow-up, results of western patients are now consistent in terms of the magnitude of OS benefit with those patients enrolled in Asia, who had a longer follow-up at the time of the primary OS analysis. No additional safety signals were noted in this current HARMONi data cut. “The positive results from this latest overall survival analysis in the global HARMONi study continue to support the translation of the therapeutic profile of ivonescimab across the globe, including western patients from North America and Europe,” stated Dr. Maky Zanganeh, President and Co-Chief Executive Officer of Summit. “We have made this updated analysis available to the FDA as we continue to progress our BLA filing for the potential approval of ivonescimab in the U.S.” “As we have consistently stated, the ivonescimab clinical trial data across multiple histologies and tumor types have repeatedly portrayed a consistent message: ivonescimab has the opportunity to make a significant difference in the lives of patients with cancer,” added Robert W. Duggan, Chairman and Co-Chief Executive Officer of Summit. “Ivonescimab continues to demonstrate its potential to increase duration of life with a tolerable safety profile. With four positive Phase III studies and clear consistency between Asian and western patients demonstrated in the global HARMONi study in the gold-standard endpoint of overall survival, we believe that ivonescimab can represent the next generation of solid tumor cancer therapy through its differentiated bispecific design.” About EGFR-Mutated NSCLC Lung cancer is the second most commonly diagnosed cancer worldwide and remains the leading cause of cancer-related death globally, with an estimated 2.6 million new cases and 1.9 million deaths in 2024.1 In the United States, the American Cancer Society estimates that approximately 230,000 new lung cancer cases will be diagnosed and nearly 125,000 deaths from lung cancer will occur in 2026.2 Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is the most common type of lung cancer, representing approximately 80% to 85% of all cases.1,3 EGFR mutations are among the most common actionable oncogenic drivers in non-squamous NSCLC, occurring in approximately 10-15% of patients in western populations and 40-50% of patients in Asia.4,5 Activating EGFR mutations can drive tumor growth through aberrant EGFR signaling.6 EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), including third-generation EGFR TKIs, are an important treatment approach for patients with advanced EGFR-mutated NSCLC.4 Despite advances with EGFR-targeted therapy, most patients with locally advanced or metastatic EGFR-mutated NSCLC eventually experience disease progression after treatment with a third-generation EGFR TKI.7 In patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC previously treated with a third-generation EGFR TKI, treatment options remain limited, underscoring the need for new therapeutic approaches after progression on EGFR-targeted therapy.7 About Ivonescimab Ivonescimab, known as SMT112 in Summit’s license territories, North America, South America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and Japan, and as AK112 outside of Summit’s license territories, is a novel, potential first-in-class investigational bispecific antibody combining the effects of immunotherapy via a blockade of PD-1 with the anti-angiogenesis effects associated with blocking VEGF into a single molecule. By design, ivonescimab displays unique cooperative binding to each of its intended targets with multifold higher affinity to PD-1 when in the presence of VEGF. This is intended to differentiate ivonescimab as there is potentially higher expression (presence) of both PD-1 and VEGF in tumor tissue and the tumor microenvironment (TME) as compared to normal tissue in the body. Summit believes ivonescimab’s specifically engineered tetravalent structure (four binding sites) enables higher avidity (accumulated strength of multiple binding interactions) in the TME (Zhong, et al , iScience, 2025). This tetravalent structure, the intentional novel design of the molecule, and bringing these two targets into a single bispecific antibody with cooperative binding qualities have the potential to direct ivonescimab to the tumor tissue versus healthy tissue. The intent of this design, together with a half-life of 6 to 7 days after the first dose (Zhong, et al, iScience, 2025) increasing to approximately 10 days at steady state dosing, is to improve upon previously established efficacy thresholds, side effects, and safety profiles associated with prior approved drugs to these targets. Ivonescimab was engineered by Akeso Inc. (HKEX Code: 9926.HK) and is currently utilized in multiple Phase III clinical trials. Over 4,000 patients have been treated with ivonescimab in clinical studies globally, and over 70,000 patients when considering those treated in a commercial setting in China, as noted by Akeso. There are currently 15 Phase III clinical studies that are either announced, ongoing, or have been completed studying ivonescimab, four of which are Summit-sponsored global studies, one of which is a multiregional study sponsored by a cooperative group, and 10 of which are being or have been conducted in China by Akeso. Summit began its clinical development of ivonescimab in NSCLC, commencing enrollment in 2023 in two multiregional Phase III clinical trials, HARMONi and HARMONi-3. In 2025, Summit began enrolling patients in HARMONi-7. Summit expanded its Phase III clinical development program into colorectal cancer (CRC) in the fourth quarter of 2025 by initiating enrollment in HARMONi-GI3. HARMONi is a Phase III clinical trial evaluating ivonescimab combined with chemotherapy compared to placebo plus chemotherapy in patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC who were previously treated with a third-generation EGFR TKI (e.g., osimertinib). Detailed results of the study were provided in September 2025, and a Biologics License Application (BLA) was submitted to the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for marketing authorization, which the FDA accepted for filing in January 2026; the goal Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) date is November 14, 2026. HARMONi-3 is a Phase III clinical trial evaluating ivonescimab combined with chemotherapy compared to pembrolizumab combined with chemotherapy in patients with first-line metastatic, squamous or non-squamous NSCLC, irrespective of PD-L1 expression. The clinical trial is evaluating the two histologies as individual, separately powered cohorts with independent statistical powering. HARMONi-7 is a Phase III clinical trial evaluating ivonescimab monotherapy compared to pembrolizumab monotherapy in patients with first-line metastatic NSCLC whose tumors have high PD-L1 expression. HARMONi-GI3 is a Phase III clinical trial evaluating ivonescimab in combination with chemotherapy compared with bevacizumab plus chemotherapy in patients with first-line unresectable metastatic CRC. ILLUMINE is a Phase III study being conducted by GORTEC, a cooperative group dedicated to Head and Neck Oncology, in recurrent / metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (r/m HNSCC). ILLUMINE is a three-arm Phase III clinical trial designed to evaluate ivonescimab monotherapy, as well as ivonescimab in combination with ligufalimab, Akeso’s proprietary anti-CD47 monoclonal antibody, compared to monotherapy pembrolizumab in patients with PD-L1 positive r/m HNSCC. In addition, Akeso has had positive read-outs in three single-region (China), randomized Phase III clinical trials, HARMONi-A, HARMONi-2, and HARMONi-6, for ivonescimab in NSCLC, including a statistically significant overall survival benefit in both the HARMONi-A and HARMONi-6 studies, and a manageable safety profile in each study. HARMONi-A was a Phase III clinical trial which evaluated ivonescimab combined with chemotherapy compared to placebo plus chemotherapy in patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC who have progressed after treatment with an EGFR TKI. HARMONi-2 is a Phase III clinical trial evaluating monotherapy ivonescimab against monotherapy pembrolizumab in patients with locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC whose tumors have positive PD-L1 expression. HARMONi-6 is a Phase III clinical trial evaluating ivonescimab in combination with platinum-based chemotherapy compared with tislelizumab, an anti-PD-1 antibody, in combination with platinum-based chemotherapy in patients with locally advanced or metastatic squamous NSCLC, irrespective of PD-L1 expression. Akeso is actively conducting multiple Phase III clinical studies in settings outside of NSCLC, including biliary-tract cancer, triple-negative breast cancer, head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, small cell lung cancer, colorectal cancer, and pancreatic cancer. Ivonescimab is an investigational therapy that is not approved by any regulatory authority in Summit’s license territories, including the United States and Europe. Ivonescimab was initially approved for marketing authorization in China in May 2024. About Summit Therapeutics Inc. Summit Therapeutics Inc. is a biopharmaceutical oncology company focused on the discovery, development, and commercialization of patient-, physician-, caregiver- and societal-friendly medicinal therapies intended to improve quality of life, increase potential duration of life, and resolve serious unmet medical needs. Summit was founded in 2003 and the company’s shares are listed on the Nasdaq Global Market (symbol "SMMT"). Summit is headquartered in Miami, Florida, with additional offices in Palo Alto, California, Princeton, New Jersey, Dublin, Ireland, and Oxford, UK. title: Hybrid Office Design: Planning Space Around How People Actually Show Up
summary: See how to design hybrid offices around measured attendance data, not headcount, using peak-day and space-mix findings from the Occupancy Intelligence Index.
body_text: The 9th edition of the Occupancy Intelligence Index found that the average office holds steady at 9-11% capacity usage, right up until midweek, when peak usage climbs to 52-60%. That gap, planned capacity sitting mostly empty except for the two or three days it overflows, is the clearest sign that the floor plans workplace teams inherited from 2019 were never built for how modern hybrid teams work. Real estate remains one of the largest controllable expenses most enterprises carry, and a floor plan that doesn't match measured attendance burns that budget on square footage nobody uses most days, or runs short on the collaboration space everyone needs on the days that matter. Hybrid office design addresses those key problems. This article walks through: What hybrid office design means when it's grounded in measured behavior rather than legacy headcount metrics How hybrid attendance changes what the office has to do A practical workflow for turning occupancy data into design decisions worth defending to finance Wondering whether your office is designed for how your teams actually work? See how 200+ global enterprises are benchmarking hybrid attendance and space demand in the 2026 Workplace Occupancy & Utilization Index. Download the Index → What Is Hybrid Office Design? Hybrid office design is the practice of shaping space, room types, desk ratios, and collaboration zones around measured attendance patterns rather than a fixed headcount number pulled from an org chart. It treats the floor plan as a live hypothesis to test against data, and revisits it as attendance patterns shift. Hybrid attendance itself takes a few common shapes across most enterprises: employees on independent flexible schedules, whole departments assigned fixed on-site days, or individual teams setting their own in-office rhythm around project needs. None of those policy structures determines the right floor plan on its own. Each produces a different attendance curve, and it's the curve that hybrid office design actually responds to. The mistake most redesigns make is skipping straight from a policy decision to a space plan, without ever measuring what the policy produced. The floor plan should follow the attendance pattern the policy produced. Why Design, Not Just Policy, Is the Lever Workplace leaders have spent the past few years tightening mandates, three days becoming four, guidance becoming a requirement, expecting attendance to follow. The 9th edition of the Occupancy Intelligence Index found what it calls the Policy Gap: stricter mandates haven't meaningfully filled offices, even where compliance improved on paper. Policy can move who shows up. It doesn't fix a floor plan built for a different era of work, and it can't manufacture the collaboration space or focus rooms that were never designed in. If the office itself doesn't support how hybrid teams actually need to work, tightening the mandate just concentrates the same design mismatch into more days. How Hybrid Work Changes What the Office Has to Do A hybrid office spends its days doing different work than a fully on-site office did. Individual desk time now competes for square footage with the moments people actually come in for: coordinated collaboration, project syncs with remote teammates, and work that's genuinely easier to do in person. That shift means the office increasingly needs collaboration-ready rooms sized and equipped for hybrid meetings, quiet focus zones for deep-work tasks that don't require anyone else in the room, and huddle spaces wired for video so hybrid teammates can loop in remote collaborators without disrupting the floor. The spaces earning their square footage are the ones built for the work hybrid teams actually do on-site . Occupancy data across enterprises tells a consistent version of this story. Demand concentrates on collaboration and meeting space, while assigned individual desks, especially ones tied to a single person who's rarely there, sit idle for most of the week. A floor plan built around 1:1 desking for every employee solves a problem hybrid offices don't have anymore, while underbuilding the one they do. How to Use Occupancy Data to Design Hybrid Offices Turning occupancy data into a hybrid office design decision follows a repeatable pattern: measure what's actually happening, read what the pattern signals about demand, then use that signal to justify a specific change to the space. Below, we walk through four moves in that pattern: allocating space based on utilization, rebalancing collaborative and individual space, planning for peak days and the midweek crunch, and revisiting geographic and portfolio needs as attendance shifts. Allocate Space Based on Utilization, Not Headcount Start with a utilization report that shows how space is actually being used, by room, by day, by hour, not how many people are assigned to a floor. Passive occupancy data catches use that badge and booking systems miss, including belongings left on a desk or a room genuinely in use with no reservation behind it. Combine that measured data with a short employee survey to capture what the numbers can't: whether a space feels too loud for focus work, or too cramped for the collaboration people are trying to do in it. Utilization data tells you what's happening; survey input tells you why it's happening , and hybrid office design needs both to right-size space types with confidence. Rebalance Collaborative vs. Individual Space Using Occupancy Trends Once utilization is measured, the mismatch usually shows up fast. A common pattern: hybrid meeting rooms running at or near peak capacity most of the week, while individual workstations down the hall sit unused for entire days. That pattern is the justification for converting underused desks into collaboration zones. Idle individual space and overloaded collaboration space are two sides of the same measurement, and closing that gap doesn't require adding square footage. It requires reallocating the square footage that's already there. Plan for Peak Days and the Midweek Crunch Hybrid attendance doesn't spread evenly across the week. The Occupancy Intelligence Index has consistently found that people compress into the same midweek hours, overflowing spaces that were sized for an average day rather than a peak one. That distinction, average versus peak, is one Kathleen Carrell, Global Workplace Strategy Leader at Takeda, has described from managing a portfolio of more than 600 buildings. Speaking at a VergeSense Occupancy Intelligence Summit, she described modeling footprint from measured demand and a utilization target rather than reverse-engineering it from headcount, an approach she calls "sizing the box before filling it." Kathleen also cautioned against designing to the outlier day, comparing it to buying a bigger house just to fit the extended family at Thanksgiving. Plan for the day you actually expect, and build flexibility into how the space operates. Hybrid office design that plans for the midweek peak is the version that holds up once the office is actually full. Revisit Geographic and Portfolio Needs as Attendance Shifts The same measurement discipline applies above the floor level. As sustained attendance data accumulates across a portfolio, not a single hiring spike or a one-quarter anomaly, patterns emerge about which sites are trending toward capacity and which are trending toward exit candidates. Portfolio right-sizing driven by that sustained data looks different from the reactive geography decisions workplace teams made a few years ago, chasing a hiring surge with a new satellite lease, then reversing it when the surge didn't hold. Right-sizing a corporate real estate portfolio works best as a standing practice, revisited every time a lease event or a material attendance shift changes the picture. Hybrid Office Design in the VergeSense Context Measuring current attendance is only half the workflow. Most workplace teams also need to plan for space they haven't built yet, or can't instrument with sensors on day one. Predictive Planning, part of the VergeSense platform, models that demand using the Large Spatial Model (LSM), trained on 250M+ sq ft of measured workplace data, letting teams simulate how a proposed layout will perform before committing capital to it. For spaces already built and in use, especially the high-value ones worth measuring continuously, conference rooms and collaboration hubs among them, the Infinity Area Sensor provides occupancy detection without the wiring or IT lift of a hardware rollout. Wireless and battery-powered, it captures the passive occupancy that badge data and booking systems miss. 4,160 Hours of Ghosted Meetings Eliminated: Consulting Firm Avoids a Floor Lease at Hudson Yards A global management consulting firm at Hudson Yards was staring down a familiar hybrid-design problem: consultants complained they couldn't find an open conference room, and the workplace team was preparing to lease another floor to add more meeting space. Occupancy data combined with room booking data told a different story. Of 10,400 hours booked into conference rooms, 40% were ghosted, blocked on the calendar by consultants who were more likely on the road than in the office and never released the reservation. The real capacity gap was in visibility into how the rooms were actually being used, which is precisely the design problem hybrid offices run into when booking data stands in for occupancy data. Using VergeSense Space Booking Automation, the firm began automatically releasing rooms when attendees didn't show. That single change eliminated 4,160 hours of ghosted meetings a month, freed up the conference room capacity the team thought it lacked, and avoided roughly $50K a month in additional leasing costs. No new floor required. What the Data Says About Hybrid Offices in 2026 The 9th edition of the Occupancy Intelligence Index measured 2025 attendance across 200+ global enterprises and 50 countries, and it names three gaps between what workplace leaders planned for and what employees actually experienced: The Policy Gap : stricter attendance mandates haven't meaningfully filled offices; tightening the rule moved compliance more than it moved actual attendance. The Space Gap : demand for different space types has outpaced supply, and that mismatch compounds as it moves across the portfolio. The Stability Gap : leadership turnover cascades directly into the space decisions that affect employees, undermining planning built on the assumption of a stable mandate. Average capacity usage held between 9-11% globally, while peak usage reached 52-60%, concentrated in the same midweek window across every region and industry the Index measured. A floor plan sized to the average is, by definition, sized wrong for the days that matter most. The space mismatch shows up sharply in the collaboration numbers. Enclosed collaboration space, only about 8% of the average office's footprint, ran at roughly 77% occupied capacity, with an 18% shortage rate during the midweek 2 p.m. peak, while open focus space, 69% of the footprint, sat around 85% occupied on average. The rooms hybrid teams need most are the smallest share of most floor plans. How to Get Started With Data-Driven Hybrid Office Design Turning this into action doesn't require redesigning the whole portfolio at once. Start by establishing a utilization baseline for the spaces you already have: measured occupancy by room type, day, and hour, not assumptions carried over from a pre-hybrid floor plan. From there, identify the space-type mismatches the baseline reveals: which collaboration spaces are running over capacity, which individual desks are sitting idle, and where the gap between booked and actually-used space is widest. Model the demand for any redesign before committing capital to it, so the layout reflects where attendance is heading, not just where it's been. Only then does it make sense to redesign, with the baseline, the mismatch, and the modeled demand all pointing at the same set of changes. That sequence is what separates a defensible hybrid office design decision from a guess dressed up as a floor plan. None of this has to start from scratch. The Occupancy Intelligence Index gives workplace leaders a benchmark for where their own portfolio stands against measured peers, and it's worth checking where the gaps in your own floor plans line up with the ones the data has already found. Want to see how your portfolio's hybrid attendance compares before your next redesign? Use the Index Explorer to filter measured utilization from 200+ enterprises by industry, region, and day of week. Explore the Data → FAQs About Hybrid Office Design What's the Biggest Mistake Companies Make When Redesigning for Hybrid Work? The biggest mistake companies make when redesigning for hybrid work is tightening attendance policy without checking whether the space itself works. Stricter mandates haven't meaningfully filled offices, and even where they do, a floor plan mismatched to real demand still leaves teams frustrated: too much individual desking and too little collaboration space. Measure the mismatch before changing the policy again. Do You Need Sensors to Start Redesigning for Hybrid Work? No, you don't need sensors to start redesigning for hybrid work. Tools like Predictive Planning can model scenarios from a floor plan, headcount, and policy inputs alone. Sensors become valuable once you want to validate a redesign against real occupancy and track how attendance patterns shift over time. How Often Should a Hybrid Office Layout Be Reassessed? A hybrid office layout should be reassessed continuously. Attendance patterns shift with policy changes, headcount growth, and seasonal variation, so a layout that fit six months ago may already be mismatched. Treat utilization measurement as standing infrastructure, and revisit the layout whenever a lease event or attendance shift changes the picture.

title: Ouster’s Commitment to the Responsible Use of Lidar Technology | Ouster
summary: Sensing and Perception for Physical AI. Digital lidar sensors for high-resolution, long-range use. Rev8: Colorized, Ruggedized, Maximized. Shipping today.
body_text: Ouster is a U.S. company on a mission to build a better future through the adoption of lidar technology, which has the potential to greatly benefit society. Lidar is a core contributor to advancements in artificial intelligence and autonomy that improve safety, quality of life, efficiency and sustainability. We also recognize that lidar technology could be misused, particularly by state and government actors. We believe we have a responsibility to prevent this type of misuse, and we expect our employees to share in this responsibility. As such, we are publishing this set of Engagement and Responsible Use Principles to help guide our work. These principles capture our commitment and decision-making to date to consider the holistic impact our products will have on communities, and convey our support for the protection of national security, civil liberties and human rights. Ouster’s Engagement and Responsible Use Principles We consider the holistic impact our products have on communities. We are committed to conducting business in a socially responsible and sustainable way in order to contribute to a better society. We continuously seek to maximize the positive impact of our products and to mitigate potential misuse. We maintain a clear policy regarding the use of our products for military and security applications. We understand that nations have legitimate security interests that require the use of lidar technology. Security, however, must be balanced with other human rights, including the rights to life and liberty. In line with the U.S. State Department’s Political Declaration on Responsible Military Use of Artificial Intelligence and Autonomy, we believe military use of AI and autonomy capabilities must be accountable via a responsible human chain of command and control. We intend to make lidar technology available only to the militaries of the United States and other free and fair nations whose interests align with the United States, provided that the applications do not (1) use our technology as the object detection, fire control and/or targeting technologies for weapons systems; and/or (2) violate laws, rules, regulations, treaties and conventions on combat and war. We do not sell our products to adversaries of the United States or repressive regimes. We are aware that some governments use lidar technology for military applications adverse to the national security interests of the United States and for surveillance applications in violation of human rights. Our employees are required to conduct diligence with the goal that all direct recipients of our technology and their applications do not violate our policy. We will cease to supply customers, partners and resellers that violate our policy. We engage in policy and regulatory efforts to support laws, policies, and standards aligned with our values. Integrity, transparency and nonpartisanship are core to our business philosophy. We partner with governments, civil society organizations and industry associations to advance laws and policies that promote the responsible and ethical use of lidar technology. This Commitment does not in any way modify, amend or replace the Company’s Code of Business Conduct and Ethics (the “Code”), and in the event of any questions of interpretation, the Code will control.

title: What to Do With a $5 Million Inheritance
summary: A $5 million inheritance often includes investments, retirement accounts, real estate and trusts. Learn how to navigate taxes and create a plan.
body_text: Inheriting $5 million can be a tremendous financial opportunity, but financial planning is still important. With more assets and tax considerations to take into account, it can help to plan ahead. As a result, understanding what you’ve inherited and how you might minimize tax consequences may have as much of an impact on your wealth as investing right away. Do you have questions about how to handle a windfall? Speak with a financial advisor today. Understand What You Inherited A $5 million inheritance is rarely a single check. More likely, it’s a mix of assets, each with their own rules for taxes, liquidity and long-term planning. Before making any financial decisions, it can help to create a complete inventory of what you’ve inherited, and identify how each asset is titled. This can help when it comes time to determine whether it’s subject to distribution rules and what type of tax treatment applies. Because larger estates tend to be more complex, it’s common to inherit several asset types at once. Understanding each one separately can potentially help you minimize mistakes and prioritize the most immediate decisions. With a larger inheritance , the challenge is often less about choosing investments and more about coordinating multiple asset types with different tax rules and timelines. Taking inventory first help build the foundation for every decision that follows. Accounting for Taxes One mistake heirs may make is assuming all inherited assets are taxed the same way. With a $5 million inheritance, that misconception can become especially expensive. Here’s what you need to know about the taxes for each type of asset that you might inherit: Asset Type Key Considerations Taxable brokerage account Review the cost basis, which may receive a step-up in basis at the original owner’s death, potentially reducing future capital gains taxes. Traditional IRA or 401(k) Determine whether you’re subject to required distribution rules under the SECURE Act, as inherited retirement accounts follow different tax rules than taxable investments. Roth IRA Qualified withdrawals are generally tax-free, but inherited Roth accounts may still have distribution deadlines. Real estate Confirm the property’s current market value, ownership structure and any ongoing expenses such as taxes, insurance or maintenance. Business interest Review governing agreements, valuation documents and any restrictions on ownership transfers or future sales. Trust assets Identify whether the trust is revocable or irrevocable , who controls distributions and whether assets remain inside the trust or pass directly to beneficiaries. Cash and bank accounts Verify beneficiary designations and decide how much should remain liquid for taxes, debt payments or near-term expenses. Because the tax rules for inherited retirement accounts are complex, and vary depending on factors such as your relationship to the deceased and whether required minimum distributions apply, a thoughtful withdrawal strategy can make a substantial difference in how much of the inheritance you ultimately keep. Click Your State to Get Matched With Financial Advisors That Serve Your Area Choose your state and answer some questions to get matched with up to three fiduciary advisors that serve your area. Planning for the Future Once you’ve accounted for taxes and understand what you’ve inherited, the next step is deciding how the assets fit into your financial plan. You may want to start by setting aside enough cash for any near-term expenses, taxes or planned purchases. From there, your investment strategy could reflect your time horizon and long-term goals, rather than the emotions that often accompany a large inheritance. A financial advisor can help you build a tax plan. Speak with an advisor today. While a $5 million estate is generally below the current federal estate tax exemption , some states impose their own estate or inheritance taxes with much lower thresholds. Depending on where you live and where inherited assets are located, those rules may influence future planning decisions. The goal isn’t simply to invest the inheritance; it’s to organize it into a coordinated strategy that supports your priorities while accounting for taxes, liquidity, long-term wealth preservation and more. Working with a financial advisor and tax professional can help you coordinate complex assets, reduce taxes and build a strategy that preserves your inheritance for years to come. title: Superside vs. Design Pickle: which creative partner is right for your team?
summary: Which platform offers what your team needs, Superside vs. Design Pickle? Compare pricing, services, AI capabilities, support and more to find the best fit.
body_text: TL;DR Superside and Design Pickle are both subscription creative services, but they're built for different teams. Design Pickle is a flat-rate, queue-based service for high-volume graphic design, completed one request at a time. Superside is the world's leading AI-first creative partner, built to give enterprise teams strategic, multi-format creative at scale through a dedicated team, and this comparison breaks down pricing, workflows, AI, services and reviews so you can match the partner to the problem. The creative bottlenecks in your workflow keep growing . Leadership expects you to support more channels, more formats and faster campaign cycles, yet your team hasn't grown in years. You're far from alone. Our research shows that 4 in 5 marketing and creative teams are at or over capacity , and seven in ten creative leaders say their internal teams are burning out. At the same time, there's little sign the pace of marketing is slowing. If anything, the demand for more creative output is only speeding up. It's no surprise, then, that more teams turn to enterprise creative subscription services. Two names that come up often in that search are Superside and Design Pickle . While both offer creative subscription services, they're built for different kinds of teams, workflows and business needs. This article compares the two, looks at how each platform works, what each does best, what they cost and where they differ, so you can make an informed decision based on your team's needs. Superside vs. Design Pickle at a glance Let's look at the big picture before we dig into the details. Differences Superside Design Pickle Best for Enterprise and mid-market teams with high creative volume Smaller teams, agencies and solopreneurs needing high-volume graphic design Model Flexible subscription; dedicated creative team running multiple workstreams in parallel Platform subscription with reserved creative hours; queue-based workflows Talent Global team across 60+ countries Global; team size depends on the creative hours in your plan Services 20+ specialized, AI-first creative services, including motion, video and ad creative Graphic design across formats like apparel, logos, web and presentations, plus motion graphics and video editing Creative leadership Dedicated creative team with strategic direction built in Execution-focused AI integration AI-powered creative management platform; 50+ workflows; 90%+ AI-certified team; custom brand models Native AI features to accelerate creative asset production Turnaround Built for fast-paced campaigns and high-demand seasons, with parallel workstreams First drafts in about 24 hours, subject to the daily creative hours on your plan Pricing Predictable, custom monthly pricing Platform tiers (Base and Pro); pricing depends on daily creative hours and commitment length Platform Superspace, a built-in PM and collaboration system with an AI layer called Brand Brain Dashboard for submitting and tracking requests; features vary by plan Reviews G2 4.5 out of 5 G2 4.4 out of 5 What is Superside? If your business has outgrown traditional agencies and freelancers, or wants to put AI to work without building all the required infrastructure from scratch, Superside is your best option. As the world's leading AI-first creative partner , we help in-house marketing and creative teams at many of the world's top brands scale high-quality, on-brand creative fast . Every project runs through Superspace , our AI-powered creative management platform. This is where all briefs, reviews, feedback and delivery live. At the heart of the platform is Brand Brain , an AI layer that captures and applies the nuances of your brand, voice, visual rules, specs, past work and team preferences. Brand Brain powers every brief and review, so creative stays on-brand from day one. While AI is applied everywhere it counts during the creative workflow, our team of senior creative talent brings creative and strategy together so the work performs across channels, formats and markets. And because we cover a range of creative services, from ad creative and video to branding , web and design systems , under a single flexible subscription , you get to replace fragmented vendors and disconnected tools with a single AI-first creative engine built for scale. The proof: more than 12,000 of our 200,000+ projects have been AI-powered , delivering approximately 35% greater efficiency. A commissioned Forrester Total Economic Impact study also found that Superside customers achieve a 94% ROI and recoup their subscription investment in less than six months. Customers: Intuit, Forter, Amazon, DoorDash, Reddit and many more . What is Design Pickle? Design Pickle is a subscription-based creative platform built around reserved daily creative hours. The model is simple: submit your unlimited design requests and revisions for a predictable monthly fee. Work is managed through a queue, with each request assigned to the designer or creative specialist best suited to the task, whether that's graphic design, illustration, presentation design, motion graphics or video editing. The company's pricing combines a platform subscription with reserved creative hours, starting at two hours per business day . You can increase those hours as your workload grows, and higher-capacity plans include additional support such as production coordinators and art directors. Because the hours are reserved for your team each day, unused capacity doesn't roll over . The service is aimed primarily at small marketing teams, agencies and solo operators who need a consistent stream of creative production but don't want to hire multiple designers. While the queue-based workflow is efficient for ongoing production, it becomes less effective when you need multiple large campaigns, highly strategic creative work or several complex projects to run simultaneously. You can purchase more hours to increase output, but Design Pickle is still designed to manage work through a prioritized queue. How Superside and Design Pickle compare head to head Now let's take a closer look at how the two compare across the seven criteria marketing teams usually consider. 1. A dedicated team vs. a queue This is the foundational difference. With Design Pickle, requests move through a prioritized queue and are assigned to the creative best suited for each task. For a steady flow of production tasks, that's simple and predictable. Superside assembles a dedicated creative team around your brand, including designers, dedicated project managers, strategists and other specialists. This means multiple workstreams can run in parallel, while a single team owns every brief end to end, from strategy through QA to delivery. 2. Talent and creative leadership Design Pickle's core talent base is a production team that executes design requests at volume, with art directors owning creative oversight and brand alignment on the more comprehensive plans. Superside, in turn, offers campaign strategy services , so every asset is sharpened against your marketing and business goals. Our global team spans far more than designers: art directors, motion artists, videographers, writers, developers and brand strategists, recruited from top agencies and brands. For enterprise brands, that thinking layer is often the entire point. 3. Services and scope Design Pickle focuses primarily on production-oriented creative services. The company is strongest in graphic design, presentations, custom illustration, motion graphics and video editing. In contrast, Superside offers 20+ specialized creative services within a single subscription. These span static and motion design , video production , branding , web design , design systems , copywriting , campaign strategy and much more. 4. AI integration Design Pickle has added native AI features to help streamline its workflows and speed up production. Superside, by contrast, is AI-first by design , not as a layer added on top. Being AI-first means AI isn't just powering individual tools. It's embedded across the entire creative model, from how teams are trained to how brand knowledge compounds over time. If you make Superside your creative team's creative team , every project runs through Superspace . Brand Brain , which sits at the system's core, serves as the AI layer that understands your brand, creative context, past decisions and previous work. Together, Superspace and Brand Brain speed up the work and reduce bottlenecks, so high-quality, on-brand designs ship from the start. AI amplifies rather than replaces human creativity. Brand strategy, creative direction, taste and judgment stay firmly human-led, while AI handles repetitive tasks and accelerates production. More than 90% of our creatives are AI-certified and supported by over 50 AI-powered workflows that help them deliver faster, more consistent, on-brand creative. In 2025 alone, our AI-enhanced workflows saved customers more than 31,000 hours and improved delivery efficiency by approximately 35%. Our own rebrand is proof that our AI-first, human-led model produces work that's both creatively ambitious and commercially effective. 5. Turnaround time and reliability Both services are quick. Design Pickle provides first drafts in about 24 hours and completes most requests within one to two business days. The timeline depends on the task's position in the queue and the creative hours you've purchased. For example, a 10-hour project could take five business days if your plan includes only two creative hours per day. Superside also delivers standard production work quickly. The difference is that, because we run parallel workstreams, you're never stuck behind a single task in a queue. The same caveat applies to both services: turnaround scales with complexity, so an original video or a new brand system takes longer than a couple of social media graphics. 6. Pricing and value Design Pickle has a lower entry price and offers month-to-month subscriptions with no long-term commitment . Pricing depends on the daily creative hours you purchase and the length of your commitment, with monthly, quarterly and annual options. Superside takes a different approach. Every subscription is tailored to the customer's creative needs, team size and objectives, giving access to a broader range of creative services, strategic support and AI-powered workflows. Rather than competing on the lowest monthly price, we're designed to help enterprise marketing and creative teams produce more high-quality work, reduce operational bottlenecks and scale without adding headcount. The return is documented too: the Forrester study found a 94% ROI with payback in under six months. For teams measuring creative on outcomes rather than unit cost, that's the number that matters. 7. Best fit by team size and creative volume Design Pickle suits smaller teams, agencies and solo operators whose work is mostly graphic design at a manageable, one-at-a-time pace, and who want a low entry point. Superside works well for enterprise marketing teams that regularly launch high volumes of creative across many formats, channels and markets at once. Curious how Superside compares to freelancers, agencies and in-house creative teams? Here's what Superside can offer your brand. Is Superside or Design Pickle right for your team? Both Superside and Design Pickle have a place in the market. The question is which service best matches your needs. Choose Superside if: You produce high volumes of creative across multiple formats at once and can't afford to sit in a queue. You want a partner that brings strategy and creative performance thinking, not just execution. Your creative work spans video, motion, branding, web, campaigns and more.
